headline: Monitor Seasonal Access for Bonavista Peninsula Coastal Sites
reservation: Dungeon Provincial Park is generally an open-access day-use site, but visitors should distinguish this from the nearby Cape Bonavista Lighthouse, which may require separate admission. Provincial camping facilities in the region operate on seasonal booking systems; check the Newfoundland and Labrador Parks website for specific opening dates and availability. Access can be impacted by seasonal road maintenance on the peninsula.

days.title: Bonavista Shore and Sea Arches
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Bonavista town centre

stops.name: The Dungeon
stops.detail: Observe the massive collapsed sea cave and two natural rock arches carved by Atlantic wave action from the cliffside overlooks.

stops.name: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit this historic 19th-century provincial site to view the restored light tower and search for puffins or whales near the cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local peninsula loops; conditions vary by wind and visibility.
days.note: The coastal gravel roads can be narrow; maintain slow speeds near the cliff edges.

days.title: Maritime History and Geology
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from the Bonavista Harbour

stops.name: Matthew Legacy
stops.detail: Explore the full-scale replica of John Cabot's ship to understand the 15th-century voyage to these shores.

stops.name: Spillar's Cove
stops.detail: Walk the rugged coastal trails to view dramatic sea stacks that showcase the unique volcanic and sedimentary geology of the region.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for short transfers between heritage sites; conditions vary.
days.note: Weather on the peninsula changes rapidly; heavy fog may obscure coastal landmarks.

days.title: Discovery Trail Exploration

stops.name: Ryan Premises National Historic Site
stops.detail: Learn about the international cod fishery that shaped the social and economic history of rural Newfoundland.

stops.name: Elliston Puffin Site
stops.detail: Observe one of the closest land-based puffin colonies in North America from the designated viewing areas.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the drive from Trinity to Bonavista; conditions vary.
days.note: Plan for frequent stops to view the shoreline; wildlife sightings are common along the roadside.

intel.title: Gravel Lot Access
intel.text: Parking at the Dungeon is a simple gravel loop; spaces are limited during peak summer months. Ensure vehicles are parked within designated boundaries to protect the fragile coastal heath.

intel.title: Cellular Dead Zones
intel.text: Reliable signal is found in Bonavista but can drop significantly once on the coastal gravel roads. Download offline maps before departing the town center.

intel.title: Peninsula Services
intel.text: Bonavista serves as the primary hub for fuel and basic supplies. Services are sparse as you travel toward the more remote coastal coves.

intel.title: Puffin and Whale Windows
intel.text: Puffin sightings are most common from late June through August. Icebergs may be visible earlier in the season depending on the year's drift patterns.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The road into the park is typically unpaved and may be closed or impassable during winter and early spring. Always check provincial weather alerts before heading to the cliffs.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Gander International Airport (YQX) and stock up on supplies in Gander before the three-hour drive to the Bonavista Peninsula.
plan.vehicle: A standard passenger car is suitable for the main roads, though a vehicle with higher clearance may be more comfortable on the unpaved Dungeon access road; check rental terms for gravel road travel.
plan.goldenHour: Cape Bonavista Lighthouse offers an elevated perspective for sunsets, though coastal fog often dictates visibility.
